articles.title: Not glamorous, but common: how to manage dandruff at home and when to get help
articles.summary: Experts don’t know exactly what causes dandruff, but if you’re seeing light flakes on your scalp, over-the-counter products can help. You spy a scatter of white flakes on your collar. Or you’ve got an itch that won’t quit, no matter how much you wash your hair.
body: An itchy, flaking scalp is rarely dangerous, but it can be annoying. Here’s what you need to know about what might be causing your flakes, what you can do about it, and when it’s time to get help.

Dandruff is the mildest form of a condition called seborrheic dermatitis, a type of skin inflammation that usually affects the head, face or trunk. At its worst, this condition leads to patches of red skin covered in tiny, greasy scales. However, most people with dandruff have just minor scaliness and no redness, affecting only the scalp.

Experts still don’t know exactly what causes dandruff, and it’s likely there are various contributing factors. A yeast called Malassezia is a leading suspect, says James Pathoulas, an assistant professor of dermatology at the University of Minnesota medical school who specializes in hair and scalp disorders. Malassezia usually lives harmlessly on the scalp, but overgrowth has been linked with scalp inflammation.

articles.title: My deep fryer lives in a tool polycule. Here’s how to stop buying things your friends already own
articles.summary: The key to happiness isn’t hoarding gadgets – it’s loaning them out and buying fewer things. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: They live under your bed and in your basement, your garage and probably in that weird cabinet above the fridge that requires a stepstool.

Alton Brown calls them unitaskers: the tools and appliances that aspire to do only one thing and do it well. Pasta makers and juicers are the classics, but they exist outside the kitchen, too. Do you really need to own a post-hole digger? Seasonal candle molds?

Well yes, sometimes. Which is why so many of us have them lurking in the recesses of our homes and apartments, gathering dust while they wait for the next dinner party that requires homemade ravioli. Local tool libraries solve this problem for home projects by filling shelves with borrowable tools instead of books. But if you don’t have one near you, or just tasks beyond DIY, I have a solution anyone can try: start a tool polycule.

For years now, half a dozen friends and I have operated an informal group here in Portland, Oregon, that swaps all the insipid items that spend 364 days a year sitting unused. It’s less a library than a group of people taking a nonmonogamous view of products instead of partners (though that type of polycule is popular in Portland, too).
points: The key to happiness isn’t hoarding gadgets – it’s loaning them out and buying fewer things.

articles.title: Spectating in Style: Stars Joined Ralph Lauren for a Spectacular US Open Finals Weekend
articles.summary: Leslie Bibb, Jessica Chastain, Rami Malek, Belmont Cameli, Amy Adams, Tom Blyth, Spike Lee, and François Arnaud joined the brand for finals weekend at Arthur Ashe.
body: The US Open’s physical layout—at least within Arthur Ashe Stadium—looked slightly different this year. With tournament organizers adding some 2,000 seats to the arena’s lower bowl, Ashe’s suite levels were bumped up a floor and many were offered more real estate as a result. Ralph Lauren, the longtime outfitter of the tournament’s official apparel, made fantastic use of its new floor plan—turning its box into an ostensible remote and racquets-centric Polo Bar. Except, instead of the famed midtown Manhattan restaurant’s dark and cozy atmosphere, team RL went bright and brass-accented in Queens.
During finals weekend, Honey Deuces flowed and Coqodaq’s caviar-topped chicken nuggets arrived aplenty. Ralph Lauren even made custom packaging with the restaurant, solely for suite guests.
points: Leslie Bibb, Jessica Chastain, Rami Malek, Belmont Cameli, Amy Adams, Tom Blyth, Spike Lee, and François Arnaud joined the brand for finals weekend at Arthur Ashe.

articles.title: Elkie Brooks looks back: ‘Before I went on stage I used to drink Guinness and a few shots of brandy’
articles.summary: The singer-songwriter on her rock’n’roll past, playing second fiddle to the Beatles, and the key to being an energetic performer in your 80s. Born Elaine Bookbinder in Salford in 1945, Elkie Brooks is a rock, blues and jazz singer known as the British Queen of Blues.
body: This is me in a white jumpsuit outside the Royal Albert Hall in London. I have very few memories of the gig, but I know I would have felt daunted as it’s such a large venue. To overcome the nerves, I’d have tried to focus on the music and remembered, “It’s just another gig.”

Ever since I can remember, I have been singing, often in the bath, to my mummy. When I was seven I would get invited to sing Mr Sandman with the band that would play at weddings and barmitzvahs. As I got older, I adored Johnnie Ray and Ella Fitzgerald, then Billie Holiday, Sarah Vaughan, Dakota Staton, Esther Phillips and Aretha Franklin. The cantor at the local synagogue used to give me singing lessons, all in Hebrew and Yiddish. He was the one who taught me the correct way to project my voice.

articles.title: Post-Show, Conner Ives and his Dolls Partied Past 2 A.M. at People’s
articles.summary: Inside, pretty much everyone looked like they could have walked the Conner Ives Spring 2027 show. Alas, many of them had—even Hunter Pifer, who was helming the DJ decks at one point.
body: The first thing that one could see when pulling up to People’s—save for a big crowd dressed in all-black dying to get in the door—on Saturday after 11 p.m. was actor Jack Cameron Kay in a fitted I Work Nights t-shirt. “I need one of those,” said this party reporter—to which Frankie Carattini, the guarder of the Greenwich Village club’s pearly gates, dead-panned: “Same.”

The late late night bash was thrown in collaboration with Jimmy Choo, who had kitted out models in footwear for the catwalk. “I’m so happy we could host him after his homecoming,” Carattini said, referring to the New York-born, London-based designer on the occasion of his inaugural NYFW outing.

Ives’s dolls—if you know, you know—were out in force. So were Paloma Elsesser, Louisa Jacobson, Troye Sivan, Precious Lee, and Ivy Getty, who invited him to the Met Gala two years back. And Alexa Chung, promising she was only staying for a few minutes but promptly making herself at home for hours, who was in the now-famous fur-trimmed silk opera coat coveted by so many.
points: Inside, pretty much everyone looked like they could have walked the Conner Ives Spring 2027 show.

articles.title: Always Read the Care Label! Inside Poshmark’s Dry Cleaner Party During NYFW
articles.summary: Elizabeth von der Goltz, Poshmark’s Chief Revenue Officer, hosted a downtown preview of the platform’s now-open-to-the-public NYFW activation, which also marks the launch of the new Try Yourself On brand campaign.
body: Upon arrival, guests were welcomed into a replica of a classic dry cleaner—complete with a working garment conveyor. Out back, a speakeasy-style cocktail lounge and showroom awaited. The idea for the set-up, which echoes the campaign imagery, came from people’s tendency to bring only their most rare and treasured items to be professionally cleaned.

In this spirit, ambassadors from the new Tastemakers campaign—think: Chloe Fineman, Courtney Grow, Colleen Allen, Jalil Johnson, Elissa Santisi and her daughter Francesca Keller—had lent pieces from their personal wardrobes to create a special NYFW collection. (You can also now follow them and shop their pre-loved pieces in the app.) Crowd favorites included a pair of feather-trimmed Prada mules, a beaded Phoebe Philo-era Chloé bag, and a Roberto Cavalli Spring 2003 mini dress that was—much to everyone’s disappointment—not for sale.

articles.title: Alexander Zverev Beats Ben Shelton to Take the US Open Men’s Singles Title
articles.summary: In a gripping four-set match, Zverev wins his second Grand Slam.
body: Number-one seeded Alexander Zverev of Germany triumphed over the big American hope, eighth-seeded Ben Shelton, in Arthur Ashe Stadium to take the US Open men’s singles title 6-3, 7-6, 5-7, 6-2. The match was both hard-fought and historic: Shelton was the first Black man to play in the final of the US Open since the stadium’s namesake, Arthur Ashe, in 1972.

The packed crowd cheering Shelton on included Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez Bezos, Katie Holmes, Rami Malek, Eiza González, Camila Cabello, Tate McRae, Martha Stewart, Adam Driver, Brad Pitt and Ines de Ramon, Lauren Bush Lauren and David Lauren, Tommy Hilfiger, Lin-Manuel Miranda, Sombr, Chris Pine, a trio of Knicks (Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart, and Jalen Brunson), and a host of tennis legends including Stan Smith, four-time US Open women’s champion Martina Navratilova, and five-time US Open men’s champion Jimmy Connors, who presented the Tiffany winner’s trophy to Zverev.
points: In a gripping four-set match, Zverev wins his second Grand Slam.

articles.title: 43 Easy 30-Minute Dinner Ideas for Busy Nights
articles.summary: Gochujang chicken, sizzling shrimp, sheet-pan gnocchi, and 40 more ways to get dinner on the table fast.
body: When you need dinner on the table fast, these 30-minute dinner ideas deliver. They’re the recipes Bon Appétit editors turn to when it’s 7 p.m., we’re already hungry, and we haven’t even made it home yet.

But quick doesn’t have to mean boring. These easy 30-minute meals include spicy chicken lettuce wraps, sizzling shrimp fajitas, creamy carbonara, crispy tofu with peanut sauce, and plenty of one-pan dinners that minimize cleanup. Some lean on smart shortcuts like rotisserie chicken, canned tuna, or store-bought dumplings; others take advantage of naturally quick-cooking ingredients like shrimp, ground meat, tofu, and eggs.
Every recipe here can be made in 30 minutes or less, start to finish. Really pressed for time? Our 15-minute meals round-up includes even speedier options.
